subject: Customer reference pressure and proposed rotation / opt-out policy
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bennett <lauren.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Customer reference pressure and proposed rotation / opt-out policy

Team —

We've been seeing a lot of repeat requests for the same handful of references (Acme, FinTechX, Northwell) from our reps and AEs — folks are getting close to burning through goodwill. Two customers explicitly asked us to pause reference asks for Q3 during renewals.

Quick summary of the problem:
- High-touch accounts are getting >3 reference asks per quarter (demos, RFPs, case study requests).
- CS and the customer success managers are having to negotiate exceptions; that consumes time and increases friction.
- We risk customers saying "no" publicly or escalating, which would hurt future reference availability.

I attached a draft policy + a CSV with a proposed opt-out column from CS. I want to propose a lightweight rotation and opt-out system we can operationalize from Sales + CS:

Proposed bullets (initial):
- Standardize a 90-day cooling period after a public reference (call/demo/case study) before we ask that customer again.
- Maintain a live rotation list per industry vertical (1°/2° references) and a short substitute list for last-minute asks.
- Require AE to check a central "reference status" doc (linked) before outreach; CS must approve in 24 hours.
- Offer small incentives for references (e.g., dedicated product feedback session + early opt-in to betas) where appropriate.

Please review the attached draft and the opt-out CSV from CS. I'm looking for a practical policy we can roll out this month with minimal legal friction. Can we lock in a policy and a lightweight operational process (who owns the rotation doc, where it lives) by EOB Friday 7/16?

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Sales Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Customer reference pressure and proposed rotation / opt-out policy

Ben — great start. A few practical notes from the field:

1) Timing constraints: 90 days is OK for most customers, but for enterprise renewals we should allow a single supervised exception if CS confirms the customer is comfortable (documented opt-in).
2) Substitute list: we should maintain a fast "on-call" pool of customers that agreed to be short-notice refs. These should be incentivized (coffee cards + short product roadmap session).
3) Incentives: legal flagged paid incentives in the past — keep to non-monetary where possible.

One ask: can we add a simple Slack workflow where AE posts the request to #refs-ops and CS can ack/deny quickly so we don't chase spreadsheets? That will speed approval. If CS is swamped, the request should default to "defer" (i.e., AE must choose substitute).

Happy to pilot with the FinTech vertical (Tom's stack). I can reach out to 2–3 substitutes this week if we finalize the wording.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Sr. Account Executive, FinTech & Payments

Thanks — I reviewed the draft. A few legal / privacy notes:

- Consent: Any customer listed as a reference must have explicit opt-in recorded with date and the context of consent (case study vs. ad-hoc reference call). The "opt-out" CSV must have timestamped confirmation.
- Incentives: Confirm non-monetary and document value (e.g., "Beta session" documented in statement of work or separate MOU).
- Public quotes: For case studies we need a separate sign-off doc.

Operational recommendation: centralize consent records in a shared Drive folder (read-only for AEs) and ensure CS tags the HubSpot contact with the reference status (ref_ok / ref_optout / ref_cooling). That will make checks programmatic.

I can help with a short template for consent capture. Avoid language that implies any financial consideration unless Procurement signs off.

Ava
Ava Chen | Counsel, Legal & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Folks —

Thanks for the quick reviews. I've incorporated the legal consent items and Marissa's operational items into a final, minimal policy. High-level changes since draft:
- Cooling period: 90 days standard; documented exception process for renewals (CS must submit exception in Drive, visible to legal).
- Live rotation: Marissa will own the vertical "on-call" substitute pool for FinTech and keep the list current in the shared Drive.
- Slack workflow: engineering will build a simple /ref-check bot in #refs-ops that reads HubSpot tags and returns status (target: pilot by 7/28).
- Opt-out capture: CS will update HubSpot contact with ref status and add timestamped row to the CSV. Ava will add the one-paragraph consent template.

Next steps: Marissa to confirm substitute contacts for FinTech (2 names) by 7/21. CS to confirm opt-out entries for Acme and any other customers by 7/22. I'll publish the final policy doc and send a brief Park & Share to sales.

Ben
